state_summary: Round 5 contains 493 observed records, 2837 eligible candidates, no pending records and no validation/test truth. Latest measurements resolve several previous questions: low-loading m211 retains late completion at 50/1; m120's large loading contrast disappears at 1/1; and m82 completion barely changes with increased loading at 20/1. Large prospective errors remain in alcohol, acetoxybenzaldehyde, acid and conjugated-ketone solvent responses. Further information should distinguish response transitions and ratio-dependent loading effects while extending transferable support across ordinary Row chemistry.
important_observations:
Observed measured evidence—m211: at 54.3 mg, endpoints change from 28.88/47.57 mL at 20/1 to 26.27/81.78 at 50/1 (434e465cfa7e0034f233, 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4). Late completion survives low loading, while onset decreases slightly. At 50/1, increasing loading to 162.9 mg gives 46.44/103.28 (0f06772820e6693753e3), a displacement of approximately +20.18/+21.51 mL. Interval width changes only from 55.51 to 56.84 mL. Revise the earlier confounded-tail interpretation toward a weak-eluent completion increase plus a loading-associated displacement of both endpoints; its causal mechanism remains untested.

Observed measured evidence—m90: the matched 110.7 mg curve measures 14.42/29.27, 30.71/60.60 and 48.17/107.99 mL at 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 (0460dfc4e1747f0fc92c, 855832bd4005ac7abdc6, 96710afeabc594baa359). The historical 10/1 completion prediction was 25.19 mL too early despite relatively accurate 5/1 completion. Previous nitrogen overprediction does not establish moderate continuation across ratios.

Observed measured evidence—m120: at 1/1, 55.65 and 166.95 mg give nearly equal endpoints, 10.54/16.67 versus 10.62/17.23 mL (2bd6619109218dcf6580, 880646809d9f015053f6). At 2/1 those same doses give 19.89/29.02 versus 8.03/10.83 (4ee22742c686bdbb1cb9, a5f9f0327623c4752e2e). Thus the loading-associated decrease is ratio dependent in the recorded comparisons. Correct the earlier memory: the higher-loading 5/1 record uses 111.3 mg, not 166.95 mg; it measures 14.67/19.14 versus 50.73/71.53 at 55.65 mg (e4fd83fb3852eb354a66, 71abc36775b6cce56da7). Saturation, dissolution and injection effects remain competing hypotheses.

Observed measured evidence—related alcohols: m119 at 105.8 mg rises from 11.83/19.31 at 1/1 to 48.00/77.09 at 5/1 (25ffcaa2164643e082b9, 776ee2c1e85ebde75168). Naphthylethanol m205 at 49.5 mg rises from 10.51/25.36 to 54.52/89.72 over those ratios (b1fcf9bf2e03028d2ef8, 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2). Its existing 99 mg 1/1 record is later, 18.27/33.28 (2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8), opposite to m120's loading direction at 2/1. Nitro-substituted phenethyl alcohol m200 rises from 15.15/37.40 to 33.88/74.44 between 1/1 and 2/1 at 64.585 mg (97318de99bab4460cf4e, a92f7617b135de150588). These results support connectivity- and condition-dependent alcohol responses without a common hydroxyl or loading correction.

Observed measured evidence—beta-ketoesters: at m82 20/1, increasing loading from 102.9 to 154.35 mg changes 26.33/64.40 to 24.23/64.37 mL (61090cfdcf019e0891a3, b6bf451b4911ee22d4a4). Completion is nearly unchanged and onset moves earlier by 2.10 mL. m94 likewise has relatively stable completion across tested 20/1 doses, with larger onset differences (ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f, e3a799d0fa90b649a157, ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4). The previous m82 loading question is locally resolved; another extensive family grid has reduced marginal value.

Observed measured evidence—ordinary oxygenated graphs: acetoxybenzaldehyde m28 rises from 6.27/25.12 at 2/1 to 39.13/81.40 at 10/1 under unchanged 116.8 mg/DCM loading (5522a1ec1f8e39cedb13, 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a). Historical 10/1 underprediction was 29.18/57.87 mL. Conversely, weak-eluent predictions for bromomethylenedioxyarene m6 and bromonitrobenzene m201 were too late (d5fd79e96156bc59e3fe, d6faa7e77464f5f9a34b). Shared acceptor counts or aromaticity cannot supply one correction.

Observed measured evidence—m68 and m27: fixed-dose m68 completion measures 12.58, 25.62, 19.59 and 17.50 mL at 2/1, 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1, with onset about 5.35–6.08 (e3716bf7dba67a0f2185, c4b06a6e718225cb9cf8, f1e08c239f1c0950ad36, cb534927304d5c892100). Added points preserve a recorded completion maximum near 5/1 without establishing its cause or same-input reproducibility. New m27 2/1 and 10/1 results were predicted closely (59d8c3d932aece6945ae, f5e5ad6e9b48aa9731b5), reducing immediate continuation value after its earlier large 20/1 failure.

Observed measured evidence—acid/ester: m45 rises from 6.63/9.00 at 1/1 to 39.58/65.65 at 20/1 (5e2f71c50a4ccaa1b83e, b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1). Its tert-butyl ester m46 changes only from 5.66/7.83 to 6.29/10.44 (84a50941febef9dc2c8f, ad98d4ead60516eb3972). The acid response includes delayed onset and interval widening, differing from cinnamic acid m173's broad strong-eluent intervals. Different masses and molar loadings prevent isolating esterification as the sole cause.

Observed measured evidence—carbonyl connectivity: dibenzalacetone m164 rises from 4.18/9.90 at 2/1 to 13.35/35.72 at 20/1 (cb729a03dac0230812b1, b7fffd840d208b29776c), rejecting its historical predicted onset decrease. Deoxybenzoin m171 and fluoroaryl ketone m65 show smaller changes across those ratios (10b3c563b748d6a9737c, 191c723f2b37d0c12afa, 0b81e78fd9712d2a9e45, 20d2b3319fd90528853f). Carbonyl-free m3's broad intervals remain separate evidence, not a carbonyl-family finding.
candidate_scientific_questions:
All following endpoints are current model predictions, not measurements.

810b065b0b86ff8c9aae: m211 at 10/1 and 162.9 mg predicts 18.25/30.42 mL. Does the loading-associated displacement measured at 50/1 occur already at 10/1? This completes a loading-by-ratio comparison with measured low-dose 10/1 and both 50/1 doses.

c76d0420b34df595c0c9: m90 at 10/1 and 166.05 mg predicts 46.30/106.88. Together with measured doses at 5/1 and the 110.7 mg 10/1 anchor, this tests whether its modest 5/1 loading effects transfer into the broad 10/1 interval.

17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec: m119 at 2/1 and 105.8 mg predicts 21.32/35.53, interpolating its matched measured 1/1–5/1 pair. c973d4c257be9ef08216: m205 at 2/1 and 99 mg predicts 19.32/32.74, almost unchanged from its measured 99 mg 1/1 anchor. 6c022e06f98c0a9771b6: m200 in pure EA at 64.585 mg predicts 6.01/14.75 and supplies a matched strong-eluent boundary. These locate distinct alcohol response transitions; the m205 comparison must not mix its 99 and 49.5 mg curves.

050e2fab4b407ea058cb and 0dccaa29989ef4956786: m28 at 175.2 mg, DCM 300 uL, predicts 16.12/38.93 at 5/1 and 38.08/79.29 at 10/1. Does its steep response persist at higher loading? The 10/1 measurement would also contrast the measured 116.8 mg anchor. The 5/1 candidate alone mixes ratio and dose relative to existing labels.

5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6: m45 at 5/1 and 85 mg predicts 20.70/33.75, matching both measured setups. Does retention develop gradually between 1/1 and 20/1, or through a localized transition?

9f450a70d44f4384353f: m164 at 5/1 and 104.77 mg predicts 5.41/15.13 between its measured anchors. a7f8c888870123f3b277: chalcone m165 at 20/1 and 107.12 mg predicts 9.78/27.69, extending its measured stronger-eluent pair. These test conjugated-ketone response transfer while retaining each molecule's measured setup.

657aa3aea4edc623ac20 and bfcb567664468f0d6902: unmeasured acetylfluorene m38 has a fixed 50 mg/DCM 1000 uL 2/1–5/1 pair predicting 3.96/16.53 to 6.98/24.54. f1dafc187f7b1ec15297 and fd9cda2d3ab32ea2a360: unmeasured biphenylaldehyde m189 has a fixed 110.7 mg/DCM 300 uL 2/1–20/1 pair predicting 4.88/14.05 to 17.59/30.69. They connect to observed fused-carbonyl and biphenyl environments while testing new onset/completion responses; m38's larger plug limits direct cross-molecule comparison.

40964ac3f659274451ef and 3fd8f569aaeff7edebea provide an unmeasured m76 bromoester 2/1–20/1 contrast at 132.9 mg. 66f42d226a5f7e934a86 and 199a9e57ec9b13740002 provide an unmeasured branched-alkyl acrylate m16 5/1–20/1 contrast at 44.25 mg. These test ordinary ester transfer beyond represented homologues; narrow predicted intervals provide no accuracy assurance.
possible_model_blind_spots: Loading effects differ in kind: m211 at 50/1 chiefly shifts both endpoints, m82 chiefly changes onset, and m120 shows a large ratio-dependent endpoint decrease. Similar HBD/HBA counts and TPSA conceal distinct adsorption environments. Current predictions have adapted around recent m28 and m200 labels but remain almost unchanged across several loading levels; acquired-condition adaptation does not establish transfer. General chemical knowledge supports silica hydrogen bonding and acid/base interactions, and stronger elution with more EA, but these are priors rather than findings about candidates. Dissolution, adsorption-site occupancy and injection effects remain untested explanations.
coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: Assess redundancy using molecule and all five supplied condition columns. Multiple catalog IDs can encode the same physical input, including already measured setups. Repeats can resolve specific ambiguities, but multiplicity and tiny mass differences do not create chemical coverage. The resolved m82 contrast and improved m27 predictions reduce the case for extensive additional local grids. Ordinary ester, ketone, aldehyde, ether and hydrophobic graphs remain relevant to overall Row accuracy alongside the recent polar failures.
warnings: Only observed-table IDs establish measured evidence. Candidate values remain predictions. Use density-derived loading_amount_mg consistently; earlier memory sometimes substituted nominal volumes or incorrect doses. Recurrence of broad m194 completion across conditions does not establish same-input reproducibility. Preserve both conflicting m73 records without identifying either as erroneous. V2 minus V1 is physical elution interval width. Crossed quantiles prevent treating reported quantile widths as calibrated uncertainty. Adaptive historical errors do not estimate unbiased overall Row error or demonstrate retraining improvement.
